draft.title: Egyptian religion and the afterlife
card: Ancient Egyptians worshipped many gods. Ra was the sun god, Osiris ruled the dead, and Isis was a goddess linked with family and magic.
Egyptians believed life continued after death. They thought a person needed a body to live on in the next life.
To keep the body from rotting, they mummified it. Embalmers dried the body and wrapped it in linen.
The dead were buried in tombs with goods for the next life, such as food, furniture and jewellery. Wealthy people could afford more goods and larger tombs.
draft.remember: Egyptians believed in life after death, so they preserved bodies and buried goods for the next life.

a.q: Why did ancient Egyptians mummify their dead?
opts: They believed the body was needed for the next life
They wanted to show how wealthy the family was
They thought it would stop the Nile from flooding
They hoped to bring the dead person back to the living
a.why: Egyptians believed life went on after death and that a person needed a body to live on. Mummifying kept the body from rotting. Wealth could affect how grand a burial was, but it was not the reason for mummifying.
a.clue: Think about what they believed happened after death.

b.q: Archaeologists open an Egyptian tomb and find jars of grain, a wooden bed and jewellery beside a mummy. What do these goods best show about the people who buried the body?
opts: They thought the dead would use these goods later
They thought the dead had worshipped only one god
They planned to take the goods back for the living
They thought the dead would be reborn as a pharaoh
b.why: Food, furniture and jewellery were placed in tombs for the dead to use in the next life. This fits a belief in life after death. Nothing in the goods points to one god, and Egyptians worshipped many.
b.clue: Ask who the goods were meant for.

a.best: They believed the body was needed for the next life

b.best: They thought the dead would use these goods later
